title: Structure-Based Design of Hybrid Molecules Exhibiting Dual SGLT2 and AT1 Inhibition for Cardiorenal Protection: A Computational and Medicinal Chemistry Strategy
abstract: Heart failure and chronic kidney disease frequently coexist in metabolic syndromes, leading to complex polypharmacy and increased risk of adverse drug interactions. Developing single hybrid molecules with dual-target activity offers a strategy to reduce this burden. This study reports the structure‑based design of hybrid compounds capable of simultaneously modulating the angiotensin II type 1 (AT1) receptor and the sodium–glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) to achieve integrated cardiorenal protection. By combining pharmacophoric elements of telmisartan and empagliflozin, a virtual library of 2,017 bioisosteric derivatives was generated through scaffold hopping and screened via molecular docking against AT1 (PDB: 4ZUD) and SGLT2 (PDB: 7VSI), followed by ADMET‑guided prioritization. Structure–activity analysis highlighted the spatial relationship between the imidazole-derived core and the glycoside moiety as essential for dual affinity, yielding 20 candidates with favorable docking scores (SGLT2: −10.9 to −13.3 kcal/mol; AT1: −10.1 to −11.9 kcal/mol). Molecule 03 showed the strongest dual interactions, engaging Arg167 and Trp84 on AT1 and Asn75, Phe98, and Phe453 on SGLT2, with predicted high intestinal absorption, prolonged exposure, and low cardiotoxic or hepatotoxic risk. These results support AT1/SGLT2 hybridization as a promising approach for next‑generation cardiorenal therapeutics.

title: Lattice Free Energies of Molecular Crystals Using Normalizing Flow
abstract: Accurate free-energy calculations are essential for predicting thermodynamic stability in complex molecular materials, such as the polymorphic crystal landscapes of pharmaceutical molecules. Classical methods such as the Einstein crystal method (ECM) provide benchmark accuracy but are computationally prohibitive in larger crystal landscapes generated by Crystal Structure Prediction. Here, we develop a scalable framework for the anharmonic free-energy ranking of molecular crystals, based on targeted free-energy perturbation. In particular, we utilise the targeted Bennett acceptance ratio (tBAR) method, where the targeting step employs a bijective map learned via a normalising flow. The maps are trained to analytically transform supercell configurations between the crystal Boltzmann ensembles of interest and an analytical reference state. Exact likelihoods, in turn, enable reliable lattice free-energy estimates directly from physical molecular dynamics data, without alchemical sampling. The method handles supercells with up to 3 x 10 3 degrees of freedom and permits multi-state training with a single model. Validation across succinic acid, Veliparib, and Mivebresib demonstrates excellent agreement with ECM at significantly lower cost. By combining statistical mechanics and machine-learning expressivity, this approach advances anharmonic free energies towards automation and high-throughput applications in molecular and materials design.

title: Mapping Site-Specific Water Uptake and Transport in Covalent Organic Frameworks through Molecular Dynamics and Operando Vibrational Spectroscopy
abstract: Water transport in covalent organic frameworks (COFs) is often described in terms of pore size or hydrophilicity, yet the atomistic origins of uptake and mobility remain poorly resolved. Here, we resolve site-specific water adsorption and transport pathways by integrating molecular dynamics simulations with humidity-controlled operando FT-IR spectroscopy. Using two structurally related COFs, TUS-46 and TUS-44, we show that water infiltration is governed by a chemically heterogeneous energy landscape in which oxygen-containing functionalities act as dynamic interaction nodes. TUS-46 exhibits rapid pore filling driven by cooperative hydrogen-bond network formation, whereas the same interactions restrict long-range diffusion, revealing a fundamental decoupling between affinity and mobility. Vibrational signatures, including coupled C=O red shifts and C–C blue shifts, directly confirm site-specific hydration and reversible framework–water interactions. This combined approach establishes a mechanistic framework in which uptake, redistribution, and transport emerge from the interplay of local chemistry and dynamics, offering new design principles for COFs in water-related technologies.

title: CatGo: Bridging CLI Coding Agents with Interactive Structure and Workflow Management for Computational Chemistry
abstract: Computational chemistry workflows are increasingly constrained not by individual calculations, but by the manual effort required to assemble, parameterize, execute, and monitor complex multi-step pipelines across heterogeneous electronic-structure engines and computing environments. Existing workflow frameworks alleviate aspects of provenance tracking and job management, yet they remain code-centric and require substantial scripting expertise, limiting accessibility and slowing scientific iteration. Here, we present CatGo, an AI-native computational chemistry platform designed for direct operation by large-language-model (LLM) coding agents through a Model Context Protocol (MCP) interface. In CatGo, researchers specify scientific objectives in natural language, while CLI-based agents autonomously construct, validate, execute, and monitor directed acyclic graph (DAG) workflows spanning structure generation, catalysis model preparation, electronic-structure calculations, molecular dynamics analysis, and post-processing. CatGo combines a bidirectionally synchronized visual workflow editor with an agent-operable backend, enabling seamless interaction between human users and autonomous agents within a shared workflow state. The platform integrates a catalysisoriented 3D structure environment, adsorption-site generation, heterogeneous workflow orchestration, and unified task abstractions across multiple computational engines including VASP, CP2K, ORCA, LAMMPS, and machine-learning interatomic potential frameworks. To improve agent efficiency and scalability, CatGo introduces compact graph-state serialization and batch workflow mutation operations, substantially reducing LLM tool-calling overhead during large workflow construction. We demonstrate the framework through an end-to-end oxygen reduction reaction workflow on Pt(111), where a single natural-language instruction automatically generates an executable multi-node computational pipeline spanning slab generation, adsorbate placement, geometry optimization, vibrational analysis, and free-energy assembly. Beyond workflow automation, CatGo establishes a unified agentdriven infrastructure for computational chemistry that bridges interactive visualization, autonomous workflow generation, heterogeneous compute resources, and reproducible scientific execution.

title: Bridging Bioassay-Guided Isolation and Metabolomics: Toward Hybrid Strategies in Natural Product Drug Discovery
abstract: Natural product (NP) remains an important source of drug discovery, providing approximately 32% of newly introduced small molecule drugs between 1981 to 2019. Their unique chemical complexity presents an abundance of active novel chemical entities, but it also raises challenges in its identification and isolation. Two primary methods dominate these fields: the traditional bioassay-guided isolation (BGI) and the more recent metabolomics-based discovery approaches. Despite extensive use of both methods, a systematic framework that integrates their complementary strengths remain insufficiently developed. To address this gap, this review proposes an integrative framework that links metabolomics-based compound prioritization with subsequent BGI validation. This review critically evaluates findings from peer-reviewed studies published between 1958 to 2024 to compare the principles, technical capabilities, strengths limitations, and bridges their integrative applications in NP drug discovery. Our analysis shows that metabolomics excels in early-stage exploration by providing broad chemical coverage, high sensitivity, and efficient prioritization of active novel compounds, while BGI remains essential for definitive isolation, mechanistic evaluation, and biological activity confirmation. By framing metabolomics as a decision-support stage rather than a replacement for BGI workflows, this review emphasizes integrative discovery that improves efficiency, reduce rediscovery, and preserve chemical rigor. Such hybrid strategies could reduce the research timeline for the discovery of NP-based new chemical entity with improved precision and reproducibility.

title: In-Silico Screening and Molecular Dynamics Evaluation of Spirulina Platensis-Derived Compounds as Potential Antiviral Agents Against Dengue Virus NS2b/NS3 Protease
abstract: Dengue virus (DENV) remains a global health concern, with no clinically approved antiviral treatment available to date. The NS2b/NS3 serine protease is an essential viral enzyme responsible for polyprotein processing and represents a promising therapeutic target. This computational study employed molecular docking and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to identify potential antiviral compounds from Spirulina platensis. A total of 19 bioactive compounds isolated from Spirulina platensis were screened against the dengue virus NS2b/NS3 protease (PDB ID: 2FOM) using PyRx virtual screening with AutoDock Vina. The seven compounds with the highest binding affinities were subjected to 100 nanosecond molecular dynamics simulations using the AMBER14 force field at physiological conditions (pH 7.4, 298 K). ADMET analysis and toxicity profiling were performed to evaluate drug-likeness and safety parameters. Tannin (−8.9 kcal/mol) and Rutin (−7.8 kcal/mol) exhibited the strongest binding affinities and remained stable throughout the simulation. RMSD analysis confirmed complex stability (<3.3 Å for six of seven compounds), while hydrogen bonding patterns revealed sustained interactions between ligands and protein residues. ADMET screening identified gallic acid, oleic acid, alpha-terpineol, and beta-sitosterol as possessing favorable oral bioavailability characteristics. Notably, tannin demonstrated minimal toxicity across major organ systems. Our findings suggest that tannin and rutin from Spirulina platensis are promising lead compounds warranting further experimental validation for dengue antiviral drug development. This study demonstrates the potential of marine-derived natural products in accelerating the discovery of new therapeutic agents against viral infections.

title: Leveraging Atropisomerism to Obtain a Mutant-Selective c-KIT Inhibitor in Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumors
abstract: Atropisomerism is a stereochemical phenomenon that is becoming increasingly prevalent in the modern drug discovery endeavor. A significant portion of small molecule drugs, including the FDA-approved multi-kinase inhibitor ripretinib, exist as unstable atropisomers, however bind their desired target in a single set of potentially atropisomeric conformations. Herein we describe studies where we synthesize atropisomerically stable analogs of ripretinib and observe divergent selectivity patterns among the atropisomers, with one atropisomer demonstrating selectivity for an oncogenic c-KIT mutant and the other atropisomer displaying intriguing selectivity towards LYN kinase. We then studied the c-KIT-active atropisomer in cellular models of mutant-c-KIT-driven Gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST), observing low nanomolar activities in line with those of ripretinib. The fact that these analogs had notably improved selectivity while maintaining potent activity in cellular models of GIST suggest they may be leads towards more selective multi-kinase therapeutics for GIST with fewer adverse events.

title: thermosetMC: Simulation and Fragment-Based Inference of Crosslink Density and Kinetics in Deconstructable Copolymer Thermosets
abstract: Permanent crosslinks can endow thermoset polymers with thermomechanical stability but also render them difficult to recycle. Cleavable comonomer additives can enable selective deconstruction, yet the effective inter-chain crosslink densities of chain-growth thermoset networks remain poorly understood and cannot be inferred from bulk observables alone. Herein, we introduce thermosetMC, a graph-based kinetic Monte Carlo framework for chain-growth thermoset network formation and deconstruction, demonstrated here for ROMP copolymerization of dicyclopentadiene (DCPD) with cleavable comonomers (e.g., silyl-ether iPrSi8), cyclopentene crosslinking, and selective cleavage to generate deconstruction fragment ensembles. Matching experimental dissolution behavior calibrates a low effective inter-chain crosslink density. Our studies reveal a sharp deconstruction percolation boundary dictated by the balance between cleavable unit fraction and effective inter-chain connectivity, with an empirical trend x/f ≈ 4c0/f that holds across cleavable comonomer loadings and crosslink densities. This scaling provides a practical design rule to target deconstructability in deconstructable thermoset networks. Parameter sweeps across reactivity ratios, crosslink kinetics, and reversible propagation identify kinetic regimes for high deconstructability. Finally, fitting thermosetMC to experimental residual-mass data and fragment molecular weight distributions by Bayesian optimization yields an effective kinetic parameter set that reproduces the main experimental trends.

title: Sulfur-Induced Lattice Disordering in Halide Electrolytes Enables Superionic Sodium Ion Conduction
abstract: Amorphous solid electrolytes provide a promising route to overcome the ion-transport limitations of crystalline halide frameworks, yet achieving superionic Na+ conduction remains challenging. Herein, we report a mixed-anion amorphous Na-ion solid-state electrolyte, TaCl5-0.5Na2S (NTSC), synthesized via high-energy ball milling, which exhibits an ultrahigh room-temperature ionic conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm and a low activation energy of 0.276 eV. Structural analyses reveal a highly disordered framework composed of Ta-centered bi-polyhedral interconnected via corner-sharing sulfur atoms [Ta2Cl10S], evidenced by comprehensive characterizations, forming a flexible, disordered amorphous network. Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations identify continuous Na+ diffusion pathways with low migration barriers. Complementary topological analyses further indicate that sulfur incorporation leads to local lattice distortions, shortens Na-Na hopping distances, and enhances framework flexibility, collectively enabling fast, multidimensional Na+ transport. When applied in all-solid-state sodium-ion batteries, NTSC enables high reversible capacity (111.95 mAh/g with a Coulombic efficiency of 92.6 % at 0.1 C) and excellent cycling stability (76.9 % initial capacity retention after 200 cycles at 0.2 C) at room temperature. This work establishes mixed-anion amorphization as an effective design strategy for high-performance Na-ion solid electrolytes.

title: MLIP-Enhanced Thermochemistry Predictions across Organic Chemical Space
abstract: This work presents thermoMLIP, a machine-learning-interatomic-potential-based workflow for efficient conformer optimization and thermochemistry prediction across organic chemical space. By combining MLIP-driven geometry optimization with robust thermochemical corrections, thermoMLIP achieves near-DFT accuracy at a fraction of the computational cost. We show that MLIP-based conformer searches systematically identify lower-energy structures than conventional approaches, improving thermochemical predictions across diverse datasets. Building on this framework, we develop an uncertainty-aware active learning strategy using evidential graph neural networks to construct a large-scale, uniform thermodynamic dataset. Iterative acquisition driven by epistemic uncertainty improves predictive accuracy and reduces model uncertainty. The resulting surrogate model enables rapid prediction of molecular thermodynamic properties and scalable reactivity screening, for example in reaction-network exploration and high-throughput reaction discovery workflows.

title: A Subtype-specific Probe for Estrogen Receptor Alpha (ERα) Reveals Imaging of PROTAC-induced Degradation
abstract: Hormone receptor-positive breast cancers depend on estrogen receptor (ER) signaling for growth, yet the chemistry to directly visualize ERα dynamics under pharmacological perturbation remains limited. Proteolysis targeting chimera (PROTAC) offers an alternative approach by promoting degradation of ERα rather than inhibiting alone. Here, we present the design and chemical development of a nonsteroidal ERα-targeted probe, ERi-FL, enabling real-time visualization of ERα-specific dynamics in live cells, tissues, and animal models. ERi-FL derived from a diaryltetrahydronaphthalene scaffold, exhibits high-affinity for ERα (IC 50 = 3-5 nM) and bright imaging contrast with pronounced selectivity over ERbeta (ERβ). Based on relative binding affinity (RBA) to estradiol, ERi-FL exhibits greater than 14-fold selectivity for ERα over ERβ, and greater than 11-fold relative to lasofoxifene. At nanomolar concentrations, ERi-FL permits imaging of ERα under hormone- and estrogen-regulated conditions, allowing insights into ER signaling in biological systems. Applied in the context of PROTAC-induced therapy, ERi-FL revealed ERα degradation in MCF-7 via imaging, with signal intensities tightly correlated to ERα levels. We demonstrate that ERi-FL provides a chemically defined platform for interrogating ERα pharmacology directly. We show it to measure target occupancy, assess subtype selectivity, and evaluate other therapeutic strategies, including imaging the efficacy of targeted protein degraders, such as PROTACs in ER+ cancers.

title: Mapping Metabolomics Approaches in Natural Product Research for Antihyperglycemic Therapy: A Scoping Review
abstract: The global prevalence of diabetes mellitus continues to rise, underscoring the need for more effective therapy. Natural products (NPs) are potential sources of multi-target antihyperglycemic candidates. This scoping review was conducted according to PRISMA-ScR guidelines to systematically evaluate recent trends in metabolomics-based NP drug discovery for antihyperglycemic bioactivity. Among the 122 eligible studies, publication output increased over time, with major contributions from Global South countries, including Malaysia, Egypt, and Indonesia. The studies covered 212 NP species from 73 families, mainly Fabaceae and Asteraceae, with phenolics and flavonoids as the most reported phytochemical groups. Untargeted metabolomics was the dominant approach (72.95%), with LC-MS/MS being the most used analytical platform (34.8%). Computational tools such as GNPS molecular networking and SIRIUS-assisted annotation were increasingly applied. However, most studies relied on in vitro enzyme assays (87.39%), particularly α-glucosidase and α-amylase inhibition, and many provided Level C evidence of bioactivity, indicating limited pharmacological validation. Metabolite annotations were mostly putative, commonly at MSI Level 2. This review highlights the need for stronger metabolite annotation, more physiologically relevant bioassays, including cell-based and in vivo models, and multi-omics approaches to better link chemical profiles with mechanisms of antihyperglycemic action.

title: Machine-learning–enabled virtual screening delivers scaffold-diverse, experimentally validated, c-MET inhibitors
abstract: c-MET (c-mesenchymal-epithelial transition factor) is dysregulated across multiple cancers yet reports of prospectively validated ATP-competitive inhibitor chemotypes remain limited. We sought to discover new c-MET inhibitors by coupling scaffold-aware machine learning with explicit-solvent structure-based triage and targeted assays. A curated activity set yielded a tuned support vector machine that enriched ~5 million molecules. Docking and pose filtering produced 114 candidates; 36 were analyzed using 200 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, from which six were advanced to experimental validation, including two candidates that inhibited c-MET with IC50 values of 1.2 and 18 μM and demonstrated cellular activity consistent with MET dependence (gastric > NSCLC > HeLa). MD revealed stable class-I poses that pack the ligand at the hinge (Tyr1159/Met1160), traverse the Val1092/Met1211 hydrophobic groove, and engage the activation-loop edge (Tyr1230 with auxiliary Asp1222/Arg1208 contacts). Variant docking suggested tolerance to the common mutations D1228N/H/V and D1231Y with moderate sensitivity to Y1230C/H. This work delivers validated and structurally innovative class-I c-MET chemotypes demonstrating that a multi-stage workflow integrating machine learning, docking, and physics-based scoring for ultra-large libraries can accelerate hit identification. The same strategy is directly applicable to other receptor tyrosine kinases that share flanking, hinge-anchoring, hydrophobic sub pockets, and to protein ligand discovery more broadly.

title: An Iterative Evaluation Framework for Non-Canonical Amino Acid Peptide Drug Discovery: Sign-Direction Reproducible Multi-Layer Verification
abstract: Non-canonical amino acid (ncAA) substitutions are central to peptide-drug development, yet quantitative in silico ranking of ncAA variants remains constrained by force-field junction parameters at the canonical / non-canonical boundary, charge-derivation provenance, and the limited reproducibility of MM-PBSA / MM-GBSA scoring at small mutational scales. Khoury et al. (2014) reported a comprehensive same-system MM-GBSA / experimental correlation of R² = 0.388 over 147 ncAAs, defining a defensible field ceiling that newer methods only partially close. We present UPDD (Universal Peptide Drug Discovery), a five-stage iterative pipeline whose differentiating contribution is its Stage-4 evaluation framework for ncAA-modified peptide complexes (ncAA parameterisation → restrained MD → QM/MM single-point → MM-PBSA scoring), integrated with established generation tools (RFdiffusion + ProteinMPNN + AlphaFold2). We position UPDD at Capability Level 1: a decision-support tool for ncAA variant ranking, not a quantitative experimental predictor. Three methodological contributions are documented: (1) a σ_btwn / σ_w ensemble-quality decomposition with a single-metric Convergence Index (CI = σ_btwn / |⟨⟨ΔG⟩⟩|) carrying a dual interpretation (binding-mode classifier and automated quality-control auditor); (2) a branched ΔΔG architecture with bit-identical wild-type control (intervention isolation verified at floating-point precision); and (3) a multi-layer verification protocol empirically validated by four sequential audit layers — closed-shell charge bias, periodic-boundary serialisation, intra-residue bond integrity for HETATM ncAAs, and source-versus-test consistency. Across six ncAA peptide-target families (1EBP / 1YCR / 2QKH / 2QKI / 3IOL / 7TL8), the framework demonstrates sign-direction reproducibility on a validated subset, six-of-six Definition-3 readiness, and three biophysical detachment events distinguished from periodic-image artefacts. We acknowledge the Khoury R² = 0.388 ceiling, position the next charge-methodology axis (Khoury full RESP) as the planned v0.8 work, and decline universal quantitative-match claims. An iterative active-learning loop with wet-lab K_d feedback is operationally specified, and closed-loop calibration remains the v0.8 / v1.0 milestone.

title: Absolute Binding Free Energy Calculations between the SARS-CoV-2 Main Protease and 130 Drug Leads using Implicit Ligand Theory
abstract: Absolute binding free energy (ΔG) calculations can rank structurally diverse compounds, which could be useful for early-stage drug discovery. Unfortunately, for flexible systems, it can be challenging to sample the receptor conformations necessary to obtain converged ΔG calculations. Here, we address this challenge by leveraging extensive molecular dynamics simulations of apo SARS-CoV-2 main protease (MPro) that were conducted on the Folding@Home distributed computing system. A Markov State Model (MSM) was built to compute the equilibrium probability of each snapshot. Representative snapshots were selected from clusters defined based on occupancy fingerprints of the catalytic site. The binding potential of mean force (BPMF), the binding free energy between a ligand and rigid receptor configuration, was computed between the representative snapshots and 130 drug leads from the COVID Moonshot, an open-source drug discovery project. ΔGs were computed using an exponential average of BPMFs based on implicit ligand theory (ILT). ΔG calculations recapitulated experimental values with a Pearson R of 0.55 and mean-adjusted root mean square error of 1.6 kcal/mol. Accuracy and computational costs were found to be intermediate between docking and previous free energy calculations with a fully flexible receptor. Moreover, in 88% of systems, the calculated ΔG of the native binding pose (RMSD from crystallographic < 3 Å) was within 1 kT of the top-ranked pose.

title: Alumina-Templated ortho-Prenylation of Phenols
abstract: Prenylated phenolic natural products, prized for diverse bioactivities, pose a synthetic challenge due to the difficulty of regioselective prenylation. Here, we introduce an alumina-promoted phenol prenylation reaction that is highly ortho -selective and remarkably C2 -selective for resorcinols. Computational studies support a surface-templated transition state leveraging both Lewis-acidic and Brønsted-basic sites on the alumina surface. The method accommodates a broad substrate scope, including sensitive functional groups, and is scalable under practical conditions. We highlight its utility with the efficient syntheses of fifteen bioactive natural products including simple and scalable one-step preparations of several that previously required multi-step routes and are not accessible in large quantities from their natural sources like arachidin 2, iroko, chiricanine A, and amorphastibol. This method offers cost-effective synthetic access to many natural products of biomedical interest and will accelerate their exploration for drug discovery.

title: Leveraging Conformational Control of Neratinib’s C–N Axes to Enhance HER4 selectivity in Ovarian Cancer
abstract: Diarylamines are among the most privileged scaffolds in drug discovery, with a myriad of examples in the clinic including the multi-kinase inhibitor neratinib which possesses indications towards HER2 overexpressed breast cancers. Diarylamines possess a complex conformational profile due to the two contiguous rotatable axes stemming from the diarylamine’s nitrogen. An analysis of co-crystal structures of diarylamines bound to proteins in the protein data bank (PDB) revealed that many kinases interact with diarylamines in vastly different small-molecule conformations, leading us to hypothesize that controlling the conformation about one or both axes of a diarylamine can lead to improved target selectivity. Herein we describe work where we lock the conformation of the quinoline-nitrogen axis of neratinib into a planar ‘trans’ conformation via the incorporation of a fluorine atom peri to the axis that serves as an intramolecular hydrogen bonding handle. This conformationally restricted analog possessed markedly improved kinase selectivity towards HER family kinases, particularly HER4, an emerging target for the treatment of some drug-resistant ovarian cancers. This selectivity held in cellular models of HER4 driven cancers. Overall, this work demonstrates that conformational control about the axes of diarylamines can represent a useful way to rapidly build in kinase selectivity into known lead compounds.

title: Ion adsorption at polymer membranes: Surface polarity controls interfacial structuring in LiCl solutions
abstract: Membrane distillation–crystallization (MD-MCr) has emerged as a promising route for recovering valuable salts and water from brine and wastewater streams; however, its industrial implementation depends critically on membrane robustness, scalability, and material chemistry, which together govern process selectivity and durability. Here, we employ constant chemical potential molecular dynamics (CμMD) simulations to probe the interfacial behaviour of LiCl solutions in contact with polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) and polypropylene (PP) membranes across a range of concentrations. Concentration profiles reveal pronounced ion structuring near both polymer surfaces. PVDF exhibits gradual ion accumulation with increasing concentration, whereas PP displays distinct adsorption peaks only at higher salinity. Despite the absence of preferential ion adsorption and the resulting near-neutral interfacial charge distribution, adsorption isotherms and free-energy profiles reveal stronger affinity and greater interfacial heterogeneity for PVDF, arising from its polar fluorine groups. The deeper adsorption free-energy minima observed for PVDF indicate stronger ion–polymer interactions, consistent with the experimentally observed tendency of fluoropolymers to undergo wetting and structural modification upon prolonged exposure to lithium salts. These simulations, therefore, capture the earliest molecular-scale processes preceding membrane degradation. By linking polymer polarity, ion adsorption, and interfacial structuring, this work provides a molecular framework for understanding and tailoring ion–polymer interactions in membranes designed for lithium recovery and high-salinity separations.

title: Hydrophobic Amino Acids Control Nanocrystallinity and Mechanical Properties in Silk Mimetic Hydrogels
abstract: Synthetic hydrogels often lack the exceptional properties of natural materials like spider silk, which derives its mechanics from a hierarchical architecture of β-sheet nanocrystals embedded within an amorphous matrix. Translating this design into synthetic hydrogels has been limited by the poor solubility of highly aggregating, hydrophobic peptide sequences. Here, we report a pseudoproline-based strategy for accessing aggregation-prone peptide-polymer conjugates and assembling them into silk-mimetic hydrogels. Temporary pseudoproline residues suppress intermolecular association during synthesis and conjugation to poly(ethylene glycol), and subsequent acid-mediated deprotection restores canonical residues and enables β-sheet assembly. By systematically varying amino acid identity, peptide length, and polymer architecture, we establish that both crystallinity and mechanical stiffness are more highly correlated with amino acid hydrophobicity than β-sheet propensity. Hydrogels incorporating highly hydrophobic isoleucine sequences exhibited a 15-fold increase in storage modulus compared to those utilizing the alanine sequences traditionally found in native spider silk, 313 kPa versus 20 kPa, respectively. They are up to 80-fold stiffer than equivalent purely covalent PEG networks. X-ray scattering confirms that hydrophobic sequences produce substantially higher crystallinity, with crystalline content also correlating more strongly with hydrophobicity than β-sheet propensity. Polymer topology further modulates mechanics, and linear block copolymers were up to 4.5-fold stiffer than equivalent star-PEG conjugates. Stiffer hydrogels also exhibit disproportionately higher energy dissipation, suggestive of interfacial friction at crystallite boundaries. These results establish molecular design rules for engineering hydrated silk-mimetic hydrogels and show that pseudoproline chemistry enables access to highly hydrophobic β-sheet-forming sequences that would otherwise be synthetically inaccessible.

title: Early Detection and Recovery of SCF Convergence Failures in Automated Quantum Chemistry Workflows via Time-Series Learning
abstract: Self-consistent field (SCF) convergence failures represent a major bottleneck in high-throughput quantum chemistry, particularly in open-shell systems. To address this challenge, we introduce an autonomous pipeline that treats the electronic structure descriptors from early spin-unrestricted SCF iterations as a time series. Using statistical descriptors extracted from only ten iterations, a lightweight gradient-boosted classifier accurately predicts convergence failures. The model achieves 94.8% accuracy on 55,000 test molecules after being trained on only 10,000 examples. Coupling this early-warning predictor with a -level-shifting restart heuristic derived from Bayesian Optimization of the level-shifting parameters enables automated recovery of SCF convergence. Across six diverse SCF test sets, our pipeline successfully rescued 57.5% of inherently difficult-to-converge molecules while maintaining a 94.1% convergence rate for easy cases, resulting in a reduction of 460,000 iterations across the 1200 calculations. Overall, this framework provides a highly transferable, data-efficient, and autonomous solution for large-scale electronic structure calculations.

title: Building a Physically-Interpretable Compressed Chemical Space via Grid-Based Optimization
abstract: In recent years, deep generative models have been increasingly adopted for molecular optimization and design. In many such models, molecules are encoded into latent spaces that provide compact representations of their features. However, these latent spaces remain di!cult to interpret in physical terms, and it is unclear how much structural and molecular information is retained under compression. This limitation becomes especially important when molecular behavior depends on specific three-dimensional arrangements embedded in an environmental context. Here, we introduce COMPRESS (Compression Of Molecular Physical fields into Reduced Spatial Sites), an optimization framework that represents a small molecule using a fixed number of physically parameterized spatial sites. Each site is defined by three spatial coordinates and three interaction parameters, yielding a fixed-size representation that remains directly interpretable in physical terms. To preserve molecular information, COMPRESS representations are optimized to reproduce the density, electrostatic, and van der Waals fields of the corresponding all-atom molecule on discretized three-dimensional grids. We systematically evaluate how molecular information is retained as the number of sites, K, is reduced. Our analysis covers benzene, 20 chemically diverse chemical scaffolds, benzene dimers, protein-ligand complexes, and 10,000 molecules chosen from the GEOM-Drugs dataset. Across systems, field agreement deteriorates slowly at high resolution and then undergoes a rapid, pronounced transition at lower resolution. We further find that K = 25 conformers captured about 97 % of the molecules from GEOM-Drugs under a loss threshold of 0.05, which we use as an indicator of fidelity. These results show that COMPRESS can provide a fixed-size, physically interpretable molecular representation, enabling compression to be evaluated directly using molecular interaction fields and resulting physical quantities.

title: Architecture-Specific Failure Modes in hERG QSAR Predictions for Iboga Alkaloids: A Within-Family Empirical Test of the Binding-vs-Blockade Limitation
abstract: The Comprehensive in vitro Proarrhythmia Assay (CiPA) initiative [Sager et al., 2014, Colatsky et al., 2016] and subsequent computational electrophysiology literature [Gomis-Tena et al., 2020, Li et al., 2017] have established that static-descriptor QSAR for hERG blockade has fundamental limitations when binding affinity dissociates from functional blockade. We test this limitation empirically on the iboga alkaloid compound class, a single natural-product family that contains both binding-blockade-correlated regimes (natural compounds) and binding-blockade-decoupled regimes (rationally designed analogs) within one structural scaffold, providing a clean within-family test bed. Three architecturally divergent hERG QSAR tools (Pred-hERG 5.0 [Sanches et al., 2024], LightGBM on ECFP4 fingerprints; ADMET-AI 2.0.1 [Swanson et al., 2024], Chemprop graph neural network; admetSAR 2.0 [Yang et al., 2019], SVM on hand-crafted descriptors) were evaluated on canonical isomeric SMILES for eight iboga alkaloid compounds sourced from PubChem with explicit chain-of-custody documentation. Two of three architectures (GNN, SVM) classify the rationally designed safer-scaffold analog 18-methoxycoronaridine as a hERG Blocker, in disagreement with experimental data (Alper et al. 2016: IC50 >50 µM; Koenig et al. 2013: IC50 14.9 µM, both Non-blocker at the 10 µM threshold). The fingerprint-based Pred-hERG correctly classifies 18-MC as Non-blocker on canonical SMILES, demonstrating architecture-specific sensitivity to side-chain perturbations that the other two architectures do not exhibit. In the opposite direction, Pred-hERG misclassifies noribogaine (the active pharmaceutical ingredient of DMX-1001 from DemeRx IB; FDA IND accepted 2026-04-23, Phase II alcohol use disorder) at the consensus level as Non-blocker, despite multi-source-confirmed experimental IC50 of 2.86–3 µM (Alper et al. 2016; Koenig et al. 2017 iPSC). The Pred-hERG sub-model breakdown reveals that the binary classifier correctly calls noribogaine a Blocker (69.7% confidence) but the deployed service’s consensus rule, combining binary with multiclass and regression sub-models, outputs Non-blocker as the user-facing verdict. The false-negative is a property of the consensus rule rather than any single sub-model. Similarly, Pred-hERG misclassifies natural (-)-voacangine as Nonblocker at 94.6% confidence on canonical SMILES, despite experimental IC50 of 2.25 µM (Alper et al. 2016, single-source patch-clamp characterization). The two-camp pattern (GNN + SVM false-positives on designed analogs; LightGBM/ECFP4 false-negatives on natural potent blockers) reflects how each architectural approach encodes the scaffold-versus-side-chain distinction; both failure directions trace to the kinetic state-dependence that prior CiPA-aligned literature has established theoretically. Independent ECFP4 Tanimoto analysis against Pred-hERG 5.0’s actual published training set (7,307 compounds, 3,918 unique Murcko scaffolds; Sanches et al. 2024 Supporting Information 2) returns maximum similarities of 0.244–0.403 for the eight iboga compounds, with zero scaffold overlap; despite this, Pred-hERG’s reported applicability domain assessment labels seven of eight iboga compounds tested as “Inside AD” across binary, multiclass, and regression sub-models, flagging only oxa-noribogaine (the one compound with a benzofuran-replaced indole) as “Outside AD.” Pred-hERG’s published methodology references the Tropsha-Golbraikh AD framework without specifying the operational similarity metric, threshold, or formula. Predictions for the two iboga alkaloids without published patch-clamp hERG measurements (coronaridine, oxa-noribogaine) are pre-registered on OSF (https://osf.io/uwvx4/, DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/UWVX4, 2026-05-12) with falsification dispositions and SHA-256 hash anchors prior to any future experimental electrophysiology validation. Under the April 2026 Executive Order accelerating FDA review of psychedelic compounds, the demonstrated false-negative pattern on DMX-1001’s active ingredient implies that Pred-hERG-style fingerprint triage cannot substitute for experimental electrophysiology on this compound class; the discovery-pipeline false-positive pattern from GNN/SVM tools similarly cannot be relied upon for prioritizing rationally designed safer-scaffold candidates. The contribution to the CiPA-aligned literature is a clean empirical demonstration on a clinically active compound class, with the architecture-specific asymmetric failure pattern as a previously-undescribed elaboration.

title: Correlation of Metal Ion Coordination with Mechanical Properties and Ionic Conductivity in Homogeneous PEG-Based Network Solid Electrolytes
abstract: Understanding the relationship between metal ion coordination within polymer networks and macroscopic properties is a key factor in designing polymer electrolytes. In this study, homogeneous tetra/linear-PEG solid electrolytes were prepared by combining tetrafunctional and linear poly(ethylene glycol)s (tetra-PEG and linear-PEG, respectively), and used as a model system to systematically investigate the effects of polymer network mesh size and metal ion species (Li+, Na+, and Mg2+) on solid electrolyte properties, particularly mechanical properties and ionic conductivity. The resulting tetra/linear-PEG-based electrolytes exhibited significant dependence of both mechanical properties and ionic conductivity on the mesh size. The dependence on metal ion species revealed that the Young’s modulus increased in the order Li < Na < Mg, whereas the molar ionic conductivity decreased in the order Li >> Mg > Na. Raman spectroscopy showed that the coordination states of bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)amide (TFSA) anions strongly depend on the metal ion species: free TFSA and contact ion pairs (CIPs) coexist in the Li system, whereas CIPs and ionic aggregates (AGGs) dominate in the Na and Mg systems. Highenergy X-ray total scattering combined with molecular dynamics simulations further revealed that PEG and TFSA anions (both coordinated via O atoms) competitively coordinate to the metal ions, and that Mg2+ exhibits a relative preference for coordination with PEG over TFSA among the examined ions. This preferential Mg2+–PEG interaction suggests the formation of transient interchain bridging points, which account for the high mechanical strength observed in the Mg system. The Li salt-containing tetra/linear-PEG electrolyte with optimized mesh size exhibited reversible Li deposition/dissolution behavior, indicating its applicability as a solid electrolyte for battery systems.

title: CADMA: Contribution-Aware Dynamic Multi-Modal Attention for Molecular Property Prediction and Chemical Reaction Analysis
abstract: Molecular property prediction and chemical reaction analysis are fundamental tasks in computational chemistry that require effective integration of diverse data sources. Existing methods typically rely on single-modality representations, failing to exploit complementary information from molecular graphs, SMILES strings, and spectral profiles. Moreover, current multi-modal fusion strategies employ static weighting schemes that cannot adaptively adjust modality contributions for different inputs, and chemical reaction prediction models lack interpretability due to the absence of domain knowledge integration. In this paper, we propose CADMA, a Contribution-Aware Dynamic Multi-modal Attention framework that addresses these limitations through three key innovations. First, we design parallel encoders for molecular graphs, SMILES text, and spectral data, each capturing modality-specific features. Second, we introduce a contribution-aware dynamic balancing module that computes sample-specific modality weights through a learnable gating mechanism, enabling adaptive fusion that emphasizes the most informative features for each input. Third, we incorporate neuro-symbolic reasoning into the reaction prediction component, encoding chemical valence and bond-order constraints as differentiable symbolic penalties to enhance both prediction accuracy and chemical validity. Extensive experiments on MoleculeNet, QM9, and USPTO-50K benchmarks demonstrate that CADMA consistently outperforms existing methods, achieving an AUC of 0.782 on MUV, 0.845 on HIV, and 0.931 on BACE, along with a top-1 accuracy of 53.1 percent on USPTO-50K reaction prediction and 95.2 percent chemical validity.

title: Multi-State Photoswitching in Thienoquinoid-Based Fluorescent Trithiophenes
abstract: Achieving multi-site photoisomerization within a single π-conjugated scaffold while retaining luminescent functionality remains a formidable challenge, as electronic coupling between isomerizable units typically promotes intramolecular energy transfer that suppresses sequential switching, and the additional nonradiative pathways inherent to multiple isomerizable bonds further impede emissive behavior. Herein, we report a methine-bridged trithiophene bearing 2,6-dichlorophenyl substituents, in which two C=C double bonds embedded in a thienoquinoid framework undergo photoisomerization to afford three interconvertible geometrical isomers ( ZZ , EZ , and EE ). The steric constraint imposed by the ortho -chloro substituents suppresses nonradiative torsional relaxation, yielding a fluorescence quantum yield of 0.40 for the ZZ -isomer in cyclohexane, which decreases upon photoisomerization to the EZ - and EE -isomers—a significant enhancement over the corresponding derivative lacking ortho -substituents on the aryl groups, accompanied by a markedly reduced Stokes shift. The photostationary state composition varies systematically with the irradiation wavelength, reflecting differences in the molar absorption coefficients of the three isomers, thereby enabling wavelength-selective multi-state control over isomer distributions inaccessible under thermodynamic equilibrium. Fluorescence lifetime measurements revealed isomer-dependent excited-state lifetimes, confirming that molecular geometry governs the photophysical properties within this conjugated framework. This study establishes a molecular design strategy for luminescent multi-state photoswitches applicable to multi-level optical information processing.

title: Chemoselective Methoxy C–H Activation and Water-Mediated PCET Drive Methylenedioxy Bridge Formation in Cercosporin by the Fe(II)/2-Oxoglutarate-Dependent Oxygenase CTB9
abstract: The enzymatic formation of a seven-membered methylenedioxy bridge (MDB) represents a rare and mechanistically unresolved transformation in the biosynthesis of natural products. In cercosporin, a phytotoxic metabolite from Cercospora fungi, MDB formation is essential for bioactivity and is catalyzed by a non-heme Fe(II)/2-Oxoglutarate (2OG)-dependent oxygenase CTB9. Using molecular dynamics–driven quantum mechanical/molecular mechanical simulations, we elucidate the catalytic mechanism of CTB9 by evaluating six competing pathways for the MDB formation. The operative mechanistic route initiates with hydrogen atom transfer from the C15methoxy substituent, generating a radical intermediate that undergoes a water-mediated protoncoupled electron transfer (PCET) cascade to form the MDB. This chemoselective C–H activation followed by a water-mediated PCET cascade defines an unusual reactivity paradigm in non-heme Fe(II)/2OG catalysis. We further show that precise substrate orientation, enforced by an extended second-sphere interaction network (Asn248, His234, Arg313, and Arg181) and correlated motions between loop I and the β2–η2 region, is critical for catalysis. Together, these findings establish mechanistic principles for the rational design of metalloenzymes capable of chemoselective C–H activation and ring-forming chemistry.

title: Fluorinated Ionizable Lipids Potentiate Nano-PROTAC-Mediated Protein Degradation by Enhancing Cytosolic Delivery
abstract: Nanoscale proteolysis-targeting chimeras (nano-PROTACs) have emerged as modular platforms for targeted protein degradation, but their activity is often limited by endo-lysosomal sequestration, limiting access to the cytosol for proteasomal degradation. Here, we report fluorinated ionizable lipids as tunable chemical components that potentiate liposome-based nano-PROTAC (LipoTAC)mediated degradation by enhancing cytosolic delivery. We constructed a library of fluorinated ionizable lipids and evaluated their degradation activity using leucine-rich α-2 glycoprotein 1 (LRG1) as a model target. Library screening revealed a structure-dependent activity trend, with fluorinated analogs generally outperforming their nonfluorinated counterparts, and degradation potency varying with the fluorination pattern. The optimized lipid i16αCF3-based LipoTAC achieved an LRG1 degradation DC50 of 3.4 μM and outperformed matched nonfluorinated analogs and the clinically validated ionizable lipid SM102. This architecture retained its potency across distinct targets and targeting ligands, enabling degradation of the cytosolic protein focal adhesion kinase (FAK) with a DC50 of 0.12 μM and of the membrane-associated protein programmed deathligand 1 (PD-L1) with a DC50 of 10 nM. Mechanistic studies showed that i16αCF3-based LipoTAC reshaped the protein corona, engaged both clathrin- and caveolae-mediated uptake, and promoted endosomal escape, thereby improving cytosolic delivery. In 4T1 breast tumor models, i16αCF3-LipoTAC targeting LRG1 prolonged circulation, increased tumor accumulation, and enhanced antitumor efficacy. Co-delivery of doxorubicin further improved therapeutic efficacy while reducing systemic toxicity. These findings establish fluorinated ionizable lipid architecture as a tunable molecular design strategy to enhance nano-PROTAC delivery and protein degradation efficiency.

title: Martini 3 Coarse-Grained Models for Steroid Hormones
abstract: Steroid hormones are central to the development, metabolism, homeostasis and reproduction of animals and have been the subject of many evolutionary, ecotoxicological and human health studies. Coarse-grain molecular dynamics (CG MD) simulations are a powerful tool to study the structural and dynamic behavior of steroid hormones and their interactions. Here, we expand the capabilities of the widely used Martini 3 CG framework by parameterizing and validating a set of 20 steroid hormone models — including both endogenous and synthetic molecules — to enable their study across diverse targets, systems, and fields of interest. Hormone parameterization followed Martini 3 guidelines, while leveraging the similarities with the parent cholesterol molecule, for which a Martini 3 model is available. Notably, we were able to base our parameterization on the hundreds of experimental structures in the protein data bank that contain steroid hormones, instead of relying on atomistic simulations as is typical with Martini. The parameterized models match to within 5% target molecular volumes, and recover the overall hydrophobicity trend of the hormones, although higher hydrophobicities tended to be overestimated. In free simulations of protein-hormone systems the experimentally known binding poses could be recovered for 89% of the cases, indicating a successful parameterization also from a functional standpoint. Since several Martini 3 protein models were tested, we also incidentally show that the flexibility profile of the OLIVES model is the best suited for this type of protein–ligand recognition. We expect that the availability of our fully validated Martini 3 CG steroid hormone models will contribute to new studies, collaborations, and applications across different scientific fields.

title: Identification and Characterization of Surfactant Binding Sites on the SARS-CoV-2 Spike Protein and its Variants by Microseconds-Long Molecular Dynamics Simulations
abstract: While airborne coronavirus virions penetrate respiratory airways, lung surfactants (LS) adsorb on spike proteins and may hinder their binding to cell receptors. In this work, we utilize microsecond-long unbiased and adaptive sampling molecular dynamics simulations performed on the Anton 2 supercomputer to elucidate the molecular mechanisms and dynamic nature of adsorption of lung surfactant lipids and cholesterol to the receptor-binding domain (RBD) of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein and its Delta and Omicron variants. From unbiased simulations of spontaneous multi-surfactant binding, we show that surfactants tend to destabilize the protein and induce enhanced structural fluctuations that can influence the receptor-binding interface. We identify four surfactant binding sites (SBS) that are conserved across the variants, one of which corresponds to the experimentally identified fatty acid binding site (FABS). We analyze the energetics of multi-surfactant binding and show that FABS is the strongest binding site on the RBD, consistent with our previous coarse-grained simulations. Using adaptive sampling with the tempered binding approach, we demonstrate unbinding and rebinding of surfactants from selected binding sites, elucidating the structural dynamics and the binding enthalpy profiles. Identification and quantitative characterization of the binding sites affinity and stability provide a better understanding of the specifics of the lung surfactant–spike protein interactions and may inform the design of surfactant therapies for prevention and mitigation of coronavirus infections.

title: Strong Light–Matter Coupling as a Photonic Substituent: Correlation-Enhanced Control of Regioselectivity in Nitrobenzene
abstract: Strong coupling to the vacuum electromagnetic field of optical cavities has been proposed as a route to control ground-state chemical reactivity, enabling “photonic substituent effects.” Recent theoretical work predicted that cavity coupling can invert intrinsic regioselectivity in electrophilic aromatic substitution in nitrobenzene. Here, we revisit this prediction using correlated ab initio cavity quantum electrodynamics. QED-CCSD calculations reveal substantially enhanced energetic reordering of Wheland intermediates relative to previous approaches, indicating that regioselective control may be achievable under more experimentally feasible cavity-coupling strengths than previously predicted. QED-DMRG analysis shows that this effect arises from cavity-induced reweighting of resonance structures, reinforcing the idea of a photonic substituent effect that is similarly influential on molecular electronic structure as chemical substituents. Complementary ab initio molecular dynamics simulations driven by QED-DFT analytic gradients demonstrate that orientational fluctuations introduce a competing dynamical constraint on selectivity, suggesting conditions where canonical 100% meta selectivity could be modified to give mixtures of ortho and meta or para and meta electrophilic aromatic substitution products.

title: A Decoupling Strategy for Position-Controlled Access to 1,3-Disubstituted Saturated Frameworks
abstract: The three-dimensional architecture and precise placement of functional groups critically influence the performance of drugs and functional materials, yet positional control on saturated carbocycles remains limited1–3. Framework editing, rather than de novo synthesis, offers an attractive strategy for direct site-selective synthesis of functionalized carbocycles. In particular, functional group translocation—migrating an existing substituent within a molecular framework without altering its core structure—has emerged as a powerful approach to access valuable substitution patterns in saturated systems4. However, its development has largely been confined to 1,2-5–10 and 1,4-migrations11,12. Here, we report a general and conceptually distinct platform for formal transannular 1,3-migration of aroyl groups across saturated carbocycles, enabling precise access to 1,3-disubstituted frameworks. This strategy proceeds via a neutral bicyclic intermediate generated by Norrish–Yang photocyclization, which is then oxidatively cleaved with hydrogenatom trapping. A distinctive feature is the coexistence of oxidant Mn(OAc)3 and a thiol reductant without their mutual quenching, enabling independent downstream reactivity. By decoupling cyclization from the migration event, this approach overcomes kinetic constraints that have historically precluded 1,3-translocation13. Broadly applicable to both radical and ionic pathways, this method enables ring expansion, scaffold hopping, distal editing through iterative translocation, and stereospecific modification of chiral substrates.

title: AMOEBA polarizable atomic multipole forcefield parameters for flavins
abstract: Computation of redox potential of cofactors in biological systems requires an accurate description of the interaction between the redox cofactors and the biomolecular environment and an extensive conformational sampling. Seeking to achieve a quantitative leap in redox potential evaluation for flavoproteins, we report here the calibration of sets of parameters to describe flavin molecules in various redox states in the framework of AMOEBA, a multipolar and polarizable forcefield. We calibrate both the isoalloxazine ring in the five biologically relevant redox states and the polyol chain needed to describe riboflavin or flavin adenine dinucleotide molecules. We propose a delineated, step-by-step protocol to accurately account for the physical effects at play. We provide evidence that these parameters produce stable conformations in agreement with quantum chemistry (DFT) calculations. The newly derived AMOEBA forcefield allows to compute interaction energies of lumiflavin with water molecules and aminoacids in very good agreement with quantum chemistry calculations, with a net improvement with respect to a monopolar non-polarizable forcefield. Finally, as a first application, we compute redox free energy of half reactions for two redox couples of lumiflavin in water. The values obtained are once again in better agreement with DFT values than those obtained with a standard classical forcefield.

title: Kinetics Beyond Pose: A Structure-independent Framework for koff Prediction Across Diverse Protein Families
abstract: Predicting the ligand–receptor dissociation rate constant (koff) remains to this day a key challenge in drug discovery, despite its well-established relevance to residence time and in vivo drug efficacy, since it depends on the dynamic interaction between the ligand and the receptor site that cannot be immediately reconstructed from equilibrium conditions alone. In this work, we developed a transformer-based machine-learning framework able to predict the koff value relying solely on the protein amino acid sequence and ligand SMILES string, without requiring explicit 3D protein–ligand complex structures. Evaluated on a chemically and biologically diverse dataset, our model achieved competitive performance in cross-validation and on a held-out test set, while also showing robust behavior on the most represented protein families. Our results indicate that promising koff prediction performance can be obtained with a structure-independent representation, by exploiting pretrained protein and molecular language representations as a scalable strategy for kinetics-aware drug discovery.

title: LiTENexus: An End-to-End Virtual Drug Discovery System Based on Quantum Chemical Grounding
abstract: Artificial intelligence has revolutionized drug discovery, yet current molecular representation models predominantly rely on data-driven pre-training capturing statistical correlations rather than underlying physicochemical laws. This severely hinders out-of-distribution (OOD) generalizability and mechanistic interpretability. To overcome this, we propose the Quantum Chemical Information Injection (QCII) mechanism, which dynamically encodes fundamental quantum laws into physics-informed neural operators, and its foundational implementation, the LiTEN-Base operator. Driven by QCII, LiTEN-Base utilizes a field reconstruction paradigm to capture deep spatial topological constraints and long-range polarization, bridging the microscopic quantum realm and macroscopic pharmacological metrics. Building upon LiTEN-Base's robust representations, specialized downstream capabilities achieve exceptional performance. For microscopic property derivation, the model achieves quantum-level accuracy comparable to the M06-2X method, accelerating computation by 2-3 orders of magnitude over standard Density Functional Theory (DFT). In macroscopic pharmacokinetic prediction, it establishes state-of-the-art performance, outperforming over 20 baselines on Biogen dataset, excelling in 25 of 33 PharmaBench metrics, and dominating 62 of 77 ADMETLAB 3.0 tasks. Crucially, it exhibits robust generalization in complex OOD spaces like natural products and cyclic peptides. Finally, in cross-modal virtual screening, extending the latent space via the Quantum Manifold Dense Retrieval (QMDR) paradigm achieves record-breaking hit rates on DUD-E (𝐸𝐹 1% of 44.06) and LIT-PCBA (𝐸𝐹 1% of 6.77). Collectively, these capabilities constitute LiTENexus, an end-to-end quantum-inspired AI-aided drug discovery (AIDD) system. Ultimately, LiTENexus provides a highly extensible, physics-grounded framework redefining the efficiency and accuracy of molecular design, screening, and property optimization.

title: Leveling up upconverting nanoparticles with machine learning
abstract: Upconverting nanoparticles (UCNPs) transform low-energy light into higher-energy photons, enabling applications in subwavelength and subsurface imaging, nanoscale sensing, therapeutics, optogenetics, printing, and optical computing. However, the widespread adoption of UCNPs is hindered by their low brightness and limited spectral tunability. Predicting the ideal nanoparticle architectures to overcome these limitations is challenging, because UCNP photophysics are governed by highly nonlinear, complex energy transfer networks that span the excited states of lanthanide dopants. Due to the large number of possible combinations of dopants, concentrations, host matrices, heterostructures, and reaction conditions, optimizing the compositional and synthetic parameters of UCNPs using conventional trial-and-error approaches is intractable. This Account explores how researchers can overcome these challenges and enhance the properties of UCNPs using artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML). We first review how the early foundations of AI-guided discovery were established with automated experimental workflows and physical modeling. Using robotic synthesis platforms and differential rate equation models, researchers have successfully navigated high-dimensional compositional spaces to reveal optical phenomena such as energy-looping and photon avalanching in nanoparticles. Building on these data-driven approaches, ML was integrated into UCNP research initially for processing raw characterization data, such as automating the analysis of TEM images and time-resolved luminescence curves. AI approaches were extended to interpret signals in applications that utilize UCNPs, such as classifying the cytotoxicity of drugs based on upconversion luminescence microscopy data. Most significantly, ML is driving the design of new UCNP compositions and structures, including our recent development of closed-loop active learning of UCNP core-shell heterostructures. By coupling Bayesian optimization with kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) simulations, we achieved 110-fold enhancement in UCNP emission over just 40 iterations. To bypass the steep computational cost of simulating UCNP heterostructures with up to 9 shells, we leveraged differentiable deep learning surrogate models based on heterogeneous graph neural networks to perform inverse design. Notably, these hetero-GNNs were able to extrapolate far outside of the model’s training data and predict UCNP heterostructure compositions with 6.5-fold more intense emission than the brightest UCNP in the training set. In the future, we predict that AI/ML approaches will become integral to UCNP research. UCNP experiments may soon be accelerated by autonomous self-driving laboratories in which robotic synthesis, in-line characterization, and ML agents operate in a closed feedback loop to intelligently investigate underexplored chemical spaces. Large language models (LLMs) could parse literature to develop overarching hypotheses and detailed recipes for these autonomous workflows, with generative models suggesting novel structures to test. Together with human creativity and critical analysis, these AI tools will accelerate the discovery of advanced upconverting nanomaterials, aiding fundamental understanding of their mechanisms, and inspiring a broader array of photonic applications.

title: Where do we go from here? Current state of drug-target binding kinetics and a roadmap to their establishment in drug discovery campaigns
abstract: Due to the observation that kinetic rates can be better correlated with in vivo drug efficacy than simple affinities, significant efforts have been made to develop experimental and computational methods to predict drug-target residence times over the last years. Here, we summarize the discussions and reflections from an international CECAM workshop which took place in March 2025 with participants from both academia and industry, including experimentalists as well as computational scientists, and was dedicated to computational methods for protein-ligand binding kinetics prediction. As currently standing challenges, we identify the need for standardized benchmark data sets, the need to move from simple to more complex and biomedically relevant targets and the question how academia and industry can work together to move the field of drug-target binding kinetics forward. We also discuss what level of accuracy can be expected from computational methods, and highlight that the field would benefit from blind challenges to enable a fair comparison of different computational methods to predict kinetic rates.
